348: Vaccine Act entitlement: whether the Special Master correctly required a showing of a defined and recognized injury, rejecting the claimant's argument that any medical condition suffices.
We agree with the government that the Special Master applied the correct standard.
349: Vaccine Act entitlement: whether the Special Master did not abuse her discretion in finding the claimant failed to show a defined and recognized injury (symptoms of unknown origin rather than cognizable injuries).
That conclusion was a reasonable inference drawn from the record evidence.
350: Vaccine Act causation: whether the Special Master erred by not performing an Althen causation-in-fact analysis after finding no defined and recognized injury; held no error because causation is not reached absent an injury.
We agree with the government that the Special Master was not required to perform an Althen analysis here.
712: Vaccine Act entitlement: whether J.G.'s post-MMR condition was a table encephalopathy compensable without causation proof; the special master's finding that no table injury was shown was left in place.

Regarding J.G.'s alleged table encephalopathy, the Greenbergs have pointed us to no evidence or arguments undermining the adverse finding on that issue, let alone under the demanding standard for Rule 60(b) relief.
1446: Vaccine Act causation: the special master's finding that the MMR vaccine did not cause A.M.'s injury (Althen prong two, onset of developmental delay preceding vaccination) was not arbitrary or capricious and was affirmed.

we agree with the Court of Federal Claims that "the special master based his finding that the onset of A.M.'s global developmental delay preceded his MMR vaccination on reliable evidence in the record."
1683: Vaccine Act entitlement and causation: whether the DTP vaccinations caused the minor's autism under the Althen test; the Special Master's denial of compensation was affirmed.
The Special Master, considering that evidence, drew plausible inferences and articulated a rational basis under Althen to deny the Canutos’ claim.
1881: Vaccine Act causation in fact (Althen): the court held the special master misapprehended the petitioner's medical theory and erred in rejecting causation, including on the three-week onset timeframe, so the petitioner is compensated.

In the face of this compelling evidence of postvaccination neurodevelopmental regression, the special master had no reasonable basis for concluding that K.P. did not experience the progressive neurodegeneration predicted by Frye's medical theory.
2830: Vaccine Act causation: Special Master erred by diagnosing the injury as TM alone, rejecting the undisputed GBS diagnosis, and failing to consider GBS-related evidence in the Althen analysis; vacated and remanded as reversible error.

Because TM and GBS are separate diagnoses that affect different parts of the nervous system, we find that the Special Master committed reversible error by failing to consider relevant evidence related to GBS.
3016: Vaccine Act causation under Althen prongs one and two (whether the MMR vaccine can cause autoimmune epileptic encephalopathy and whether a logical sequence of cause and effect exists). The court did not decide causation on the merits; it vacated because the special master failed to consider the full record and remanded.

We therefore vacate the decision below and remand to allow the special master to consider the entire record including the relevant medical and scientific evidence, such as Dr. Shafrir's second report and the articles cited therein.
3563: Vaccine Act causation-in-fact (Althen prongs one through three) for a non-Table injury alleged to be significantly aggravated by the FluMist vaccine; special master's denial of compensation upheld as not arbitrary or capricious.
Because H.L. failed to establish a prima facie case of causation, the burden never shifted to the government to prove otherwise.
3714: Vaccine Act causation: the special master's finding that K.A. did not experience an encephalopathy, so petitioner failed to establish causation-in-fact under Althen, was upheld.
Ms. Austin has not provided reason to set aside the Special Master's determination that she failed to show by preponderant evidence that K.A. experienced an encephalopathy.
3756: Vaccine Act entitlement and causation: Wyatt failed to prove the Fluarix vaccine caused her GBS or polyarthritis under Althen, because the GBS theory lacked reliable support and polyarthritis lacked a logical medical theory and a clear onset date. Special Master's causation findings were not arbitrary and capricious.
Wyatt does not point to any evidence that shows the Special Master's findings regarding causation were arbitrary and capricious.
4456: Vaccine Act causation: whether the FluMist vaccine caused the claimed narcolepsy under Althen, including whether the Special Master improperly required epidemiological proof and reasonably weighed the Duffy and Han studies. Denial of compensation affirmed.
The Special Master's reliance on Duffy did not improperly raise the standard in Althen beyond a preponderance of the evidence.
4717: Vaccine Act causation in fact: the special master's finding that petitioners failed to prove under Althen that the vaccinations caused W.R.'s alleged injuries (encephalopathy, autism spectrum disorder) was not arbitrary or capricious, so compensation was denied.
On appeal, we conclude, the Rogeros have not shown that these findings, which followed the established legal standards, were arbitrary and capricious.
4973: Vaccine Act causation in fact for an off-Table injury: Byrd failed to satisfy the Althen causation requirements, so compensation was denied.
The chief special master thoroughly reviewed the record and correctly determined that he had failed to do so.
5202: Vaccine Act causation under the Althen prongs: the Chief Special Master found petitioners failed to prove vaccination caused E.O.'s Dravet syndrome; the Federal Circuit affirmed.

we hold that the Chief Special Master did not misapply Daubert in weighing the parties' experts' testimony and supporting evidence and that the Chief Special Master's factual findings were neither arbitrary nor capricious.
5218: Causation evidence for reasonable basis: the Special Master's finding of no evidence of causation was clearly erroneous because K.C.'s medical records paired with the Gardasil package insert constitute objective evidence supporting causation.
We conclude that the Special Master’s finding is clearly erroneous because the record does contain objective evidence of causation supporting a reasonable basis.
5227: Vaccine Act causation: the court vacated the special master's denial of compensation because his finding that Trystan's February 16, 2009 arm contortions were consistent with a cold was unsupported by expert testimony addressing them, and remanded the Althen causation issue for further consideration.

Because this issue is of central importance to the causation analysis, it is necessary to remand for further consideration of the causation issue in light of the special master's findings in 2018 regarding Trystan's arm contortions.
5307: Vaccine Act on-table claim: whether L.M. had a QAI-defined encephalopathy pre-vaccination (acute encephalopathy requirement), so no Table injury was shown; special master's denial affirmed.
For the above reasons, we affirm the Special Master's denial of Petitioner's on-table claim.
5308: Off-table claim, Loving prong 3: special master legally erred by requiring petitioner to prove expected outcome for a DYNC1H1 mutation and that current condition was worse than that outcome.
For the above reasons, the Special Master legally erred in applying Loving prong 3.
5309: Off-table claim, Loving prong 4: special master legally erred in requiring medical literature and in rejecting petitioner's medical theory; the Ambry patient finding was arbitrary and capricious.
the Special Master's rejection of Petitioner's medical theory was arbitrary and capricious and must be set aside.
5310: Off-table claim, Loving prong 5: finding that seizures predated vaccination defeated the logical sequence of cause and effect was erroneous and set aside.
In light of this flawed reasoning, the Special Master's finding under Loving prong 5 must be set aside.
5311: Off-table claim, factor unrelated inquiry: government's finding that the DYNC1H1 mutation was the sole substantial cause was unsupported by the record and set aside.
Thus, the Special Master's factor unrelated finding must be set aside as arbitrary and capricious.
5661: Vaccine Act entitlement and causation: whether the Tdap vaccine caused Lozano's ADEM under the Althen prong two logical sequence of cause and effect; special master's causation finding upheld.
we conclude that the special master applied the correct legal standard and considered the entire record in finding that Lozano proved causation by a preponderance of the evidence.
6441: Vaccine Act causation: whether the October 1, 2009 influenza vaccine caused a significant aggravation (relapse) of J.M.'s preexisting nephrotic syndrome; special master's denial of compensation affirmed under substantial evidence review.
We find no error in the special master's determinations, and therefore affirm.
6553: Vaccine Act causation/entitlement for the 2014 aggravation claim: petitioner failed to produce sufficient medical records or other evidence to support the claim; judgment affirmed on that basis.
With respect to the 2014 claim, Ms. Gaiter has failed to produce sufficient medical records or other evidence to support her claim despite multiple requests from the Special Master to do so.
6592: Vaccine Act causation: whether the vaccinations caused J.J.D.'s death from SIDS under the Althen test, given the Triple Risk Model theory; special master's causation finding affirmed.

We find that the Special Master's factual findings were not arbitrary or capricious, and the decisions of both the Claims Court and the Special Master were in accordance with the law, specifically this court's decision in Boatmon.
6686: Vaccine Act causation under Althen prong one: whether the HPV vaccine could cause petitioner's rheumatoid arthritis; special master found petitioner failed to show a reputable medical theory, affirmed.
Thus, Ms. Olson failed to meet her burden to demonstrate causation under Althen prong one.
7051: Vaccine Act causation in fact under Althen prong one: whether the special master properly found that McCollum failed to show a medical theory causally connecting the influenza vaccine to his narcolepsy, and did not impose an improper burden.

we are unable to say that the special master erred by imposing any kind of an improper burden upon Mr. McCollum. We therefore decline to disturb the special master's finding that Mr. McCollum failed to satisfy prong one of Althen.
7316: Vaccine Act causation in fact for an off-Table SIDS death: whether petitioners proved under Althen prongs one and two that the vaccinations caused or contributed to J.B.'s death. The court held the Special Master applied a lower standard than 'reputable' and 'sound and reliable' and that the evidence did not show causation, so compensation was denied.
In this case, the Petitioners failed to prove by a preponderance of the evidence that the vaccinations J.B. received can and did cause or contribute to his death.
7508: Vaccine Act causation: whether the special master applied an impermissibly low burden of proof in finding a reputable medical theory of causation (Althen) for a non-Table injury; the government's challenge was rejected.
Thus, the government has not shown that the special master's findings regarding causation were arbitrary and capricious.
7789: Vaccine Act off-Table causation: whether Tdap vaccination caused Winkler's Guillain-Barré Syndrome under Althen, including whether the special master improperly required him to rule out an alternative infection (C. jejuni) and how the burden on alternative causation was applied.
we affirm the Special Master's holding that Winkler failed to prove causation of GBS by the Tdap vaccine by preponderant evidence.
8232: Vaccine Act causation in fact for a non-Table injury (infantile spasms) under the Althen prongs. The court held the first special master applied the correct legal standard, found her Althen findings sufficient, and held the second special master improperly reweighed the evidence, so the petitioners prevailed on causation.
We find that both Court of Federal Claims decisions were in error.
8613: Vaccine Act causation under Althen prong one: whether petitioner showed a medical theory causally connecting flu and Tdap vaccines to ADEM; not compensated.
Thus, the Special Master's conclusion that Ms. Orloski failed to prove the first Althen prong with the two submitted articles by preponderance of the evidence is supported by the evidentiary record.
9398: Vaccine Act causation: the special master found Mr. Webb's left-side Bell's palsy began before his November 20, 2012 flu vaccine, so compensation was denied for lack of causation (Althen proximate temporal relationship); affirmed as not arbitrary or capricious.
We conclude that the special master's finding that Mr. Webb's Bell's palsy began prior to his November 20, 2012 flu vaccination was not arbitrary or capricious.
9704: Vaccine Act causation in an off-Table case: the special master's finding that the petitioner did not prove Althen prong three (proximate temporal relationship), so C.L.'s chronic ITP was not shown to be vaccine-caused, was not arbitrary or capricious and was affirmed.

In view of the special master's analysis and the evidence of record, we conclude that this factual finding—that C.L.'s chronic ITP more likely than not began no earlier than May 2014—was not arbitrary or capricious.
10224: Vaccine Act causation in fact under Althen: the court held Trystan satisfied Althen prongs two and three because his arm contortions began within two weeks of vaccination and persisted, and the special master's contrary finding was arbitrary and capricious.
Accordingly, Trystan satisfied Althen prongs two and three and established causation in fact.
10225: Government's factor-unrelated defense: the Secretary did not establish that Trystan's genetic mutations were the sole substantial cause of his Leigh's syndrome, so the claimant remains entitled to compensation.
Thus, the government did not meet its burden to establish Trystan's Leigh's syndrome was the result of factors unrelated to the vaccine.
10460: Vaccine Act causation: whether the Td vaccine actually caused brachial neuritis under Althen (logical sequence of cause and effect and proximate temporal relationship); special master's finding of no actual causation affirmed.

We reject Mr. Greene's challenge to the special master's determination that Mr. Greene did not establish a logical cause-and-effect relationship between vaccine and injury by a preponderance of the evidence.
10758: Vaccine Act causation: the special master's finding that the flu vaccine did not cause the petitioner's NMOSD (Althen prongs one and two not satisfied), reviewed as arbitrary and capricious, including the underlying diagnosis of NMOSD rather than LETM.

Because Mr. Morgan was found to have suffered from NMOSD, and because Mr. Morgan has not provided sufficient evidence to support a legally probable connection between his vaccination and his NMOSD, we hold that the special master's findings on causation were not arbitrary or capricious.
11398: Vaccine Act off-Table causation: the court held the special master properly found Cerrone failed to prove by a preponderance of the evidence, under all three Althen factors, that the vaccines caused his ulcerative colitis, so no compensation is owed.
For the foregoing reasons, we uphold the special master's analysis and conclusions regarding the Althen factors and thus the ultimate issue of causation.
11562: Vaccine Act entitlement: the polysaccharide pneumococcal vaccine received by the decedent is excluded from the Vaccine Program, so no compensation is available on that claim.
such vaccine was explicitly excluded from the Vaccine Program, and it therefore does not entitle the appellant to compensation.
11563: Vaccine Act entitlement: the petitioner failed to prove receipt of the alleged influenza vaccine (a Table vaccine) by a preponderance of the evidence, and the Special Master's finding that it was not administered was not arbitrary or capricious.
the record evidence not only failed to show that Williams received an influenza vaccine, but it affirmatively showed that Williams did not receive an influenza vaccine.
11665: Vaccine Act causation under Loving factor five: whether the vaccines caused a significant aggravation of B.O.'s Dravet syndrome by a logical sequence of cause and effect; special master's weighing of evidence upheld, so entitlement denied.

Because the Chief Special Master correctly applied the law with respect to Loving factor five, and his findings of fact were not arbitrary or capricious, we do not find reversible error, and we affirm the judgment of the Claims Court.
11666: Loving factor four: the special master's apparent requirement that vaccines wholly alter the course of the disease was legal error under Sharpe and Althen, though harmless.
Thus, to the extent that the Chief Special Master imposed a higher burden, it was legal error, albeit harmless given our affirmance of his findings regarding Loving factor five.
12237: Vaccine Act causation: whether the FluMist vaccine caused V.H.'s narcolepsy under Althen prong three (proximate temporal relationship); special master found petitioners did not carry their burden, and the Court of Federal Claims sustained that denial.
we conclude that the special master's finding on Althen prong three was not arbitrary or capricious (or otherwise erroneous)
12316: Vaccine Act causation: whether A.V.'s vaccination caused or significantly aggravated her seizure disorder; the Court of Federal Claims' finding of no causation was affirmed.
On appeal, the Vinesars challenge the Court of Federal Claims' determination that the Vinesars failed to demonstrate that A.V.'s vaccination caused or significantly aggravated her seizure disorder.
12377: Vaccine Act entitlement and causation: whether Shawn received the flu vaccine (a Table vaccine) on December 21, 2015, so that compensation is owed; special master's factual finding upheld as not arbitrary or capricious.
Because the special master's finding is based on evidence in the record and is not wholly implausible, we affirm.
12444: Vaccine Act causation: the Special Master's use of the Althen factors to structure the reasonable-basis analysis was not per se legal error, and his structuring of the causation evidence was upheld.

This does not constitute per se legal error because the Althen factors can provide definitional context to causation when evaluating whether there is a reasonable basis that a causal relationship exists between the vaccine and the injury.
12723: Vaccine Act causation: whether the Claims Court erred in holding the Special Master arbitrarily and capriciously relied on the Langer-Gould study (non-statistically significant findings) as support for the Loving fourth-factor medical theory of causation of significant aggravation of MS. The Federal Circuit reversed, holding the Special Master's reliance was not arbitrary or capricious and that Doles is entitled to compensation.
SM Horner was not arbitrary and capricious in his assessment of Langer-Gould and his conclusion that it provides support for Ms. Doles' theory of causation.
13341: Vaccine Act causation: whether the DTaP vaccine caused SNHL and tinnitus under Althen; special master found causation not shown and Claims Court affirmed.
We conclude that the special master's conclusion that Herms' evidence of causation was unpersuasive was not in error.
13602: Vaccine Act causation (Althen): affirmed the special master's finding that petitioners failed to prove N.A. suffered a seizure, so the claim was not compensated.
We agree on the record as it stood before the special master that the special master did not err in concluding that petitioners did not present preponderant evidence of a seizure.
13720: Vaccine Act causation, Althen prong one: the petitioner's medical theory that the influenza vaccine can cause MS via molecular mimicry was not shown by preponderant evidence to be sound and reliable; burden-of-proof standard applied properly.
The Special Master did not err in stating that Althen prong one required "preponderant evidence of a sound and reliable theory."
13721: Vaccine Act causation, Althen prong two: logical sequence of cause and effect not shown, given evidence of another possible cause (upper respiratory infection); temporal proximity alone insufficient.
Accordingly, we conclude that the Special Master did not err in her analysis of Althen prong two, and the Court of Federal Claims did not err in sustaining the Special Master's decision.
14135: Vaccine Act causation: the court held the special master properly applied the standard that the government must prove by preponderant evidence that an unrelated factor (H. influenzae infection) was the sole substantial cause, so the petitioner's Table presumption did not require the government to eliminate the vaccine as a cause. Compensation denied.

Accordingly, while the government in a Table case must affirmatively prove that a factor unrelated was the sole substantial cause by a preponderance of the evidence, it need not disprove that which was never affirmatively proven, i.e., the vaccine as the cause in fact.
14136: Vaccine Act causation under Althen prongs one and three (medical theory and temporal relationship for the unrelated infection): the court found no reversible error in the special master's findings that the government met its burden on both prongs.
We therefore see no reversible error regarding the special master's analysis of the first prong of Althen.
14232: Vaccine Act causation-in-fact under Althen prong one: whether the special master applied the proper evidentiary standard and properly found no medical theory causally connecting the PCV (Prevnar 13) vaccine to GBS; claimant not compensated.
We conclude that the special master did not apply a standard inconsistent with Althen.
14427: Vaccine Act off-Table causation under Althen prong one: whether the petitioners proved by preponderant evidence a medical theory connecting FluMist to narcolepsy with cataplexy; Chief Special Master's denial of compensation affirmed.

We see no legal error in this analysis, as we have repeatedly explained that a petitioner must prove a medical theory by a preponderance of the evidence that a vaccination can cause a particular injury.
14823: Vaccine Act causation: the Special Master found petitioners failed to prove by a preponderance that the DTaP vaccine was a substantial factor (Althen causation-in-fact for a non-Table injury), and the Federal Circuit affirmed that finding and the claim denial.

Rather, based on the evidence presented, including the evidence that K.S.S.W. possessed two chromosomal abnormalities known to cause neurological problems, the Special Master found that Petitioners had failed to prove that the DTaP vaccine was a substantial factor in causing K.S.S.W.’s condition.
14915: Vaccine Act causation: the special master properly found the government showed the unrelated H. influenzae infection was the sole substantial factor causing GBS and excluded the flu vaccine as a causal factor.

We therefore conclude that the special master's decision to exclude the vaccine as a substantial causal factor is grounded in the relevant record evidence and supported by plausible inferences and thus it is not arbitrary and capricious.
14916: Althen prong one: the government's medical theory connecting the unrelated infection to GBS was adequate; the special master's analysis was not arbitrary and capricious and White's standard was an incorrect articulation of case law.
White's argument is therefore premised on an incorrect articulation of our case law.
14917: Althen prong three: the government showed a proximate temporal relationship between the unrelated infection and the injury; the special master's temporal finding was reasoned and not arbitrary and capricious.
we will not second guess the special master's reasoned assessment of the evidence and expert reports.
